reference.method: damped Newton at 50 digits on the README log density, from the fitted values

global.statement: With both coefficients free, every nonempty count sample has a finite maximum. If a count is positive, the maximizing pair is unique. All-zero data are maximized by $\pi=1$ with any $\lambda>0$. With $\lambda>0$ held, free inflation has a unique maximum. With $\pi<1$ held, a finite rate maximum exists whenever a count is positive, but two global maxima can tie. For all-zero data and held $\pi<1$, the supremum requires $\lambda\downarrow0$ and is not attained in the declared domain. Held $\pi=1$ permits only zeros and leaves a free rate unidentified. Holding both coefficients leaves likelihood evaluation, subject to compatibility.
global.reason: Write $z$ for the empirical zero fraction. At a held rate, the inflation maximum is $\max\{0,(z-e^{-\lambda})/(1-e^{-\lambda})\}$, with value one for all-zero data. In the positive-inflation branch, the rate solves $\lambda/(1-e^{-\lambda})=\bar x/(1-z)$, whose left side is strictly increasing. If this branch is infeasible, the unique maximum is the Poisson member $\pi=0,\lambda=\bar x$. For held $\pi<1$ and a positive count, the likelihood tends to zero at both ends of the rate domain, so a finite maximum exists. Its score has at most three roots; two separated maxima can tie.
